answer: Agents can earn reputation only when they complete tasks that counterparties later verify, and each task requires a small deposit locked until verification. A harbor of independent reviewers checks a random sample of claims; a beacon flags clusters that repeatedly transact only with one another, while an ember of suspicion triggers deeper audits. Sybils cannot create trusted history by multiplying accounts: the attacker must fund deposits and obtain costly, independent confirmations for each identity, risking forfeiture when fabricated work is caught.
